title: The Field Journal
story:
Pinned to the mess-hall corkboard, in Kip Lindqvist's loopy handwriting:

"Everyone writes the daily field journal into /workspace/journal and Tomasz wants it as a website. I made one, but I copied the files INTO the image, so every new entry needs a rebuild. Also I once typed into it from inside the container. Help??"

Serve the journal with nginx as `field-journal` on port 8085. The folder must be mounted, not copied, so new entries appear at once, and mounted read-only so the website can never alter an entry.
objectives: Run `field-journal` from `nginx:alpine` publishing port `8085` to container port 80
Writing into `/usr/share/nginx/html` inside the container must fail
startingState: The folder `/workspace/journal` holds three daily entries (`day-01.txt` to `day-03.txt`). No containers are running.
hints: A bind mount maps a host directory into a container, so edits on one side show up on the other immediately. You can also mark the mount so the container cannot write to it.
Use `-v <absolute-host-path>:<container-path>:ro` together with `-p 8085:80`. nginx serves files from `/usr/share/nginx/html`.

```bash
docker run -d --name field-journal -p 8085:80 \
  -v /workspace/journal:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro \
  nginx:alpine
curl http://localhost:8085/day-02.txt
```

files.content: DAY 01 - Landed at Kestrel Point. Wind 38 knots, gusting 52.
DAY 02 - Core drill assembled. Tomasz counted the bolts twice.
DAY 03 - First 40 metres of ice recovered. Generator coughing again.

validation.description: Writing into the mounted folder fails inside the container

debrief: Edits in `/workspace/journal` appear instantly because the container reads the host folder directly, and `:ro` keeps it a pure reader. Pro tip: bind mounts need an absolute host path; a bare name like `journal` silently creates a named volume instead.
